A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 17-page FPET paper, including Appendices A–E. Complete text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish identical substantive content. The only visible difference is the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original FPET accuracy, efficiency and ablation results on VTAB-1K, plus experiments on other backbones, full datasets, few-shot classification and cross-modal retrieval.

after.justification: v2 retains the original FPET experiments, including VTAB-1K results in Tables 1–5 and supplementary classification and retrieval results in Appendices A and B.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Figure A4 specify the same method: middle-layer token merging, checkerboard partitioning, adapter-based key refinement, straight-through estimation and gradient stopping.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 19 VTAB-1K tasks, five few-shot classification datasets, full CIFAR-100 and SVHN datasets, and Flickr30K cross-modal retrieval. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments, including the PET baselines in Tables 1–2, LTMP and ToMe comparisons, pooling alternatives, few-shot baselines and UniAdapter in Table A7.

E3.justification: Backbones, splits, sample sizes, shot counts, metrics and training budgets are unchanged. Both specify 100-epoch AdamW training and the same batch sizes and hyperparameters in Section 5 and Table A8.

E4.justification: The component ablations, merging-layer trade-offs, rank-reduction comparison and token-merging visualizations are identical in Section 5.4 and Appendix A. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Statistical and uncertainty reporting is identical throughout the experimental descriptions, tables and plots, including Figure A2. No run counts, seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 retains FPET-AdaptFormer accuracy of 76.2% and inference time of 2.12 ms; Table A7 retains FPET-UniAdapter image-to-text R@1 of 94.1.

T1.justification: The definitions and mathematical development in Sections 3–4, including Equations 1–14 and the straight-through matching formulation, are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about plug-and-play FPET improving inference speed and training efficiency while preserving parameter efficiency and competitive accuracy.

C2.justification: The explanations of gradient stopping, semantic preservation during merging and accuracy–efficiency trade-offs are unchanged. No substantive interpretation, applicability qualification or limitation is added.

D1.justification: Both provide identical pseudocode in Figure A4, hyperparameters in Table A8, dataset statistics in Table A9, hardware information and code-access statements. The code hyperlink target is unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 62 references and identical related-work discussion are retained. Positioning relative to existing PET, token-pruning and token-merging approaches does not change.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv v1 dated 26 March 2025 to v2 dated 26 August 2025. The title, authors, prose, terminology and document structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–17 are pixel-identical, and page 1 differs only in the arXiv stamp text.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, evidence, exposition and reproducibility information are identical, including all appendices. Updating the arXiv stamp and adding its self-link does not meaningfully improve or diminish the paper's overall quality.
